## Key terms

{{< glossary matrix-multiplication dot-product column-vector transformation commutative identity-matrix inverse-matrix determinant square-matrix main-diagonal >}}

## 10.1 Casting a spell: a matrix times a vector

- A spell is a 2 × 2 matrix; the crystal's position is a column vector.
- Matrix × vector: **each row times the vector** (a dot product, lecture 4).
  For the rows (a, b) and (c, d) and the vector (x, y): the result is
  (ax + by, cx + dy).
- Stretch = rows (2, 0) and (0, 3). On (4, 1): row 1 gives 2 × 4 + 0 × 1 = 8,
  row 2 gives 0 × 4 + 3 × 1 = 3. The crystal goes to **(8, 3)**.
- Turn = rows (0, −1) and (1, 0). On (3, 2): (−2, 3). (x, y) becomes (−y, x).
- One matrix moves every point of a sprite in the same way.

![Each row times the vector gives one coordinate.](images/matrix-vector.png){width=92%}

{{< sim file="sims/multiply-lab.html" poster="sims/multiply-lab.png" title="Multiply Lab: a 2 × 2 matrix moves a point and a shape" height="760" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Do not multiply entry by entry. Every row uses both x and y.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Check Turn in Multiply Lab"}
On paper, multiply Turn (rows (0, −1) and (1, 0)) by P = (2, 3). Then press
"Turn 90°" in **Multiply Lab** and drag P to (2, 3). Compare.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Matrix × vector"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(2, 15)|(6, 0)"}
What is the matrix with rows (3, 0) and (0, 1) times (2, 5)?
:   (6, 5)

What is the matrix with rows (1, 2) and (0, 1) times (1, 3)?
:   (7, 3)

Turn has the rows (0, −1) and (1, 0). Where does it send (4, 0)?
:   (0, 4)

Stretch has the rows (2, 0) and (0, 3). Where does it send (4, 1)?
:   (8, 3)

Each entry of a matrix × vector is …
:   one row times the vector
:::
:::

## 10.2 Two spells at once: a matrix times a matrix

- AB exists when A has as many **columns** as B has **rows**.
  (m × **n**) times (**n** × p) gives m × p.
- The entry in row i, column j of AB = row i of A · column j of B.
- A = rows (1, 2), (3, 0); B = rows (4, 1), (0, 2).
  AB = rows **(4, 5)** and **(12, 3)**. For example row 1 · column 2 =
  1 × 1 + 2 × 2 = 5.
- (2 × 3) times (3 × 4) gives 2 × 4. (2 × 3) times (2 × 3): no product.
- Games multiply two spell matrices once and use the result for every point.
  Grow × Turn = rows (0, −2) and (2, 0).

![Row i of A times column j of B.](images/matrix-matrix.png){width=92%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
The matrix product is not entry by entry. Each entry is a whole row times a
whole column.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · A product on paper"}
A = rows (2, 1) and (0, 3); B = rows (1, 0) and (4, 2). Compute the four
entries of AB, each as a dot product. What is the size of AB?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Matrix × matrix"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="3 × 3|rows (3, 1) and (0, 2)"}
A = rows (1, 1), (0, 2); B = rows (3, 0), (1, 1). What is AB?
:   rows (4, 1) and (2, 2)

A is 3 × 2 and B is 2 × 5. What is the size of AB?
:   3 × 5

Can a 2 × 3 matrix be multiplied by a 2 × 3 matrix?
:   no, 3 and 2 are different

The entry in row 2, column 1 of AB uses …
:   row 2 of A and column 1 of B

Why do games multiply two spell matrices first?
:   then each point is multiplied only once
:::
:::

## 10.3 First stretch, then turn: the order matters

- In general **AB ≠ BA**: matrix multiplication is **not commutative**.
- With A = rows (1, 2), (3, 0) and B = rows (4, 1), (0, 2):
  AB = rows (4, 5), (12, 3) but BA = rows (7, 8), (6, 0).
- In AB**v**, the matrix next to the vector acts first: **first B, then A**.
  Read from right to left.
- Point (2, 1): Flip then Turn gives (−1, −2). Turn then Flip gives (1, 2).

![Stretch then turn, and turn then stretch.](images/order-matters.png){width=92%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Do not read a product from left to right. In AB**v**, B acts first.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Order on paper and in the lab"}
Take the point (3, 1). Apply Flip then Turn, and Turn then Flip, on paper.
Then do the same in **Multiply Lab**, one matrix after the other.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · The order"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="always|(2, −1)"}
Is AB always equal to BA?
:   no

In AB**v**, which matrix acts first?
:   B

From (2, 1), Flip then Turn: where does the point go?
:   (−1, −2)

From (2, 1), Turn then Flip: where does the point go?
:   (1, 2)

In which order do you read a product of transformations?
:   from right to left
:::
:::

## 10.4 The spell that changes nothing: the identity

- The **identity matrix** I has 1 on the main diagonal and 0 everywhere
  else.
- I**v** = **v** and IA = AI = A: it changes nothing.
- I × (5, −2): row 1 = 1 × 5 + 0 × (−2) = 5; row 2 = −2. The point stays.
- The 4 × 4 identity is the matrix of a new object: at the origin, not
  turned, size 1. In Unity: `Matrix4x4.identity`.
- A matrix full of 1s is **not** the identity: rows (1, 1), (1, 1) send
  (5, −2) to (3, 3).

![The identity matrix leaves every point where it is.](images/identity.png){width=92%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
The identity has 1s only on the main diagonal.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · The identity in Multiply Lab"}
Press "Identity" in **Multiply Lab** and drag P to three points. Where is MP?
Then change one 0 into a 1: what happens to the house?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · The identity"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="rows (1, 1) and (1, 1)|(0, 0)"}
What is I × (7, −3)?
:   (7, −3)

Which matrix is the 2 × 2 identity?
:   rows (1, 0) and (0, 1)

Where does a new object with the identity matrix stand?
:   at the origin

Rows (1, 1) and (1, 1) times (5, −2) gives …
:   (3, 3)

What is I × A?
:   A
:::
:::

## 10.5 Undo: the inverse matrix

- The **inverse** A^−1^ undoes A: A A^−1^ = I.
- For the rows (a, b) and (c, d): the **determinant** det = ad − bc, and
  A^−1^ = (1 ÷ det) × the rows (d, −b) and (−c, a).
- Grow = rows (2, 0), (0, 2): det = 4, inverse = rows (0.5, 0), (0, 0.5) =
  Shrink. Shrink × (6, 4) = (3, 2).
- Rows (2, 1), (1, 1): det = 1, inverse = rows (1, −1), (−1, 2).
- **det = 0: no inverse.** Squash = rows (1, 2), (1, 2) sends (2, 0) and
  (0, 1) to the same point (2, 2); nothing can bring them back.
- In Unity: `m.inverse`. `worldToLocalMatrix` is the inverse of
  `localToWorldMatrix`.

![Grow and its inverse.](images/inverse.png){width=92%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
The inverse is not "1 ÷ every entry". Use the formula and check A A^−1^ = I.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Which spells can be undone?"}
Compute the determinant of: rows (4, 0), (0, 2); rows (3, 6), (1, 2); rows
(0, −1), (1, 0). Which ones have an inverse? Write the inverse of the first.
Then press "Squash" in **Multiply Lab**.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · Determinant and inverse"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="rows (0.2, 0.5) and (0.5, 1)|4"}
What is the determinant of the rows (5, 2) and (2, 1)?
:   1

What is the inverse of the rows (5, 2) and (2, 1)?
:   rows (1, −2) and (−2, 5)

What is the inverse of Grow (rows (2, 0) and (0, 2))?
:   rows (0.5, 0) and (0, 0.5)

The rows (2, 4) and (1, 2): why is there no inverse?
:   det = 0

What is A × A^−1^?
:   the identity I
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Crystal Spells {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

**Crystal Spells** is a puzzle game. The crystal starts at (2, 1). Each
spell is a 2 × 2 matrix: **Grow** = rows (2, 0), (0, 2); **Shrink** = rows
(0.5, 0), (0, 0.5); **Turn** = rows (0, −1), (1, 0); **Flip** = rows (−1, 0),
(0, 1); **Stay** = the identity.

{{< sim file="sims/crystal-spells.html" poster="sims/crystal-spells.png" title="Crystal Spells: cast the right matrix" kind="game" height="720" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 6 · One spell"}
Crystal at (2, 1). Grow = rows (2, 0), (0, 2); Turn = rows (0, −1), (1, 0);
Flip = rows (−1, 0), (0, 1); Stay = identity. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="Shrink|(1, 2)"}
Where does Grow send the crystal?
:   (4, 2)

Which spell sends the crystal to (−1, 2)?
:   Turn

Which spell sends the crystal to (−2, 1)?
:   Flip

Which spell keeps the crystal at (2, 1)?
:   Stay
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 7 · Spells in a row (harder)"}
Grow = rows (2, 0), (0, 2); Shrink = rows (0.5, 0), (0, 0.5); Turn = rows
(0, −1), (1, 0); Flip = rows (−1, 0), (0, 1). Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(2, −1)|Turn"}
Grow sent the crystal to (4, 2) by mistake. Which spell undoes it?
:   Shrink

From (2, 1): Flip, then Turn. Where does the crystal land?
:   (−1, −2)

From (1, 2): Turn, then Grow. Where does the crystal land?
:   (−4, 2)

Grow × Turn as one matrix: what are its rows?
:   (0, −2) and (2, 0)
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- Matrix × vector: each row times the vector gives one coordinate.
- In AB, each entry is a row of A times a column of B; A needs as many columns as B has rows.
- AB is usually not BA; in AB**v**, B acts first.
- The identity matrix I changes nothing: 1 on the main diagonal, 0 elsewhere.
- The inverse undoes a matrix; a 2 × 2 matrix with det = ad − bc = 0 has no inverse.
